source.title: Dynamic Cluster Data Sampling for Efficient and Long-Tail-Aware Vision-Language Pre-training
source.authors: Mingliang Liang; Zhuoran Liu; A. D. de Vries; Martha Larson

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream performance across training-sample scale in vision-language pre-training, an extension beyond language-model held-out-loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no held-out cross-entropy measurements, power-law fits, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Table 5’s own sample-scaling results bear on V6. Comparisons with other methods, including results reproduced from prior work, do not test the listed scaling-law versions and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a CLIP data-sampling method paper. Kaplan et al. appears only as a citation for VLM transferability. The study fits no scaling law and measures no held-out loss. Its 'data scaling' section (Table 5) gives three samples-seen points for its own DynamiCS method only, as evidence that the method keeps improving. It does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or loss. The system is a contrastive vision-language model, not language-model pretraining. This is the authors' own method's performance under more training, not a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors' main conclusion is that DynamiCS (cluster scaling plus dynamic per-epoch sampling) cuts VLM training cost and improves long-tail performance. The Table 5 scaling result is a secondary observation of consistent gains with more samples seen.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates zero-shot VLM task accuracy across training-sample counts, rather than fitting language-model held-out-loss scaling laws. It changes the data-sampling method and does not test parameter/token compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to sampling factor α and other DynamiCS settings, but does not show that these choices change scaling-law fits or exponents.

fits_no_version.finding: For DynamiCS CLIP ViT-B/16, zero-shot accuracy rises monotonically with diminishing increments as samples seen double from 0.64B to 2.56B. ImageNet goes 61.5/65.0/67.5 on LAION and 69.2/71.3/72.6 on DataComp-DFN (Table 5). No fit is made.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a data-sampling method in contrastive VLM pre-training, downstream zero-shot accuracy keeps increasing with samples seen over a 4x range.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 shows per-class zero-shot accuracy roughly log-linear in pretraining concept frequency, with some deviations noted by the authors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CLIP class accuracy scales log-linearly with that concept's frequency in the pretraining data.

record.problems: The relevant scale sweep covers only three reported sample-count settings per dataset and reports downstream accuracies without uncertainty estimates. It does not measure held-out loss or fit a predictive scaling relationship.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were omitted as rows. Tables comparing DynamiCS with other methods, and unrelated ablations of sampling settings, do not test the listed versions; cited results from prior work were excluded.

untested.parts: No held-out loss and no power law in parameters, tokens or compute.
No fit on small runs and no extrapolation.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Vision-language training, but no power-law form is fitted to loss or accuracy.
No test of predictability from scale or loss. Only three samples-seen points for the authors' own method, with no fit.
No exponents or fitting choices examined.

record.verdict_notes: Reader's V6 'supports' label removed. The paper is a method paper whose scale sweep covers only its own method, at three points, with no predictive law and a non-LM system. Cross-method comparisons (Tables 3, 4, 6–10) and the ViT-B to ViT-L comparison against CLIPA are method comparisons, not scaling tests.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No power law is fitted on small runs or evaluated for extrapolation to larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation between parameters and tokens is tested.
No comparison of architecture details at fixed parameter count and loss is reported.
The study uses vision-language pre-training but does not test whether a power-law form holds for held-out loss in that or another modality or training regime.
Tests downstream top-1 accuracy as the number of training samples seen increases for DynamiCS; does not test prediction from pretraining loss, fit a predictive law, or test parameter-count scaling.
No scaling-law exponents, compute-optimal split, or dependence of such fits on setup or fitting choices is examined.
